title: Fermat's Theorem on Sums of Two Squares

problemStatement.formal: p \text{ is an odd prime} \implies \bigl(p \equiv 1 \pmod{4} \iff \exists\, a\, b \in \mathbb{N},\; p = a^2 + b^2\bigr)
problemStatement.plain: Fermat's theorem on sums of two squares states that an odd prime $p$ can be written as a sum of two perfect squares if and only if $p \equiv 1 \pmod{4}$. This is one of the most elegant characterizations in elementary number theory.

# Knowledge Base: infinitude-primes-4k1-oq-01

---

## Problem Understanding

The target is Fermat's theorem on sums of two squares for odd primes: an odd prime p is representable as p = a^2 + b^2 over natural numbers exactly when p is congruent to 1 modulo 4. This is intended as a standalone strengthening around the existing infinitude-primes-4k1 gallery proof.

The source proof already imports Mathlib.NumberTheory.SumTwoSquares and uses mod_four_ne_three_of_dvd_isSquare_neg_one, so the research should begin by locating the cleanest Mathlib API rather than rebuilding the theorem from scratch.

---

## Current Evidence

- Selection report classifies the problem as tier B with significance 7/10, tractability 8/10, and EMPTY knowledge score.
- state.md remains in OBSERVE with zero attempts and no active approach.
- problem.md lists Mathlib.NumberTheory.SumTwoSquares, ZMod.isSquare_neg_one_iff, GaussianInt, and modular arithmetic as the relevant infrastructure.

---

## Insights

The only-if direction should be comparatively small: squares modulo 4 are 0 or 1, so an odd prime represented as a sum of two squares cannot be congruent to 3 modulo 4. The if direction is the hard classical theorem, but the evidence expects Mathlib to already contain a prime representation theorem or a near-direct equivalent.

The first credible implementation path is a direct wrapper around SumTwoSquares. Gaussian integers and descent remain fallback strategies if the API survey shows a gap.

---

## Dead Ends

No approaches have been tried yet.
